Location: @UUID[JournalEntry.iyojT7kJHH23BWLd]{The Glass Gallery (Elysium)}
Scenes: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.uL8F2YNogcToiFc6]{A2-E01 · Elysium Night} · @UUID[JournalEntry.doItxeK8y7M1PufU.JournalEntryPage.snrsN5RkdAklRIDn]{A4-E01 · Primogen Council}

Elysium night (A2-E01, Night 3). You enter from the plaza, to the south, through the glass doors of the lobby. Solène Marchetti, the Keeper (PNJ-14), waits there at her desk with the register open (DOC-03), and on the threshold that separates the lobby from the great hall stands the velvet tray on its pedestal: “Your phones, please.” The fourth custom of Elysium is literal: “No connected device crosses the threshold” (CIUDAD-LEYES); the threshold is the 2 m gap between the lobby and the hall, and switched-off devices are kept in the cabinet on the lobby's east wall.

The great hall of the jellyfish. “Hundreds of pieces of blown glass hang from the ceiling like frozen jellyfish, red, amber, and black, and the light that passes through them moves across the floor every time someone walks by.” The pieces hang several meters above people's heads: they aren't drawn and don't block movement; their pools of color are the hall's Foundry lights (red and amber, with a slight flicker). On the terrazzo floor there are only two low benches and three pedestals with individual pieces. With every wall made of glass, from almost any point you can see almost everything else: “the glass walls make it impossible to know who's listening from outside” (LUG-03).

The quartet nobody sees. “A string quartet nobody can see is playing”: the musicians play in the west alcove, which opens onto the hall through a gap covered by a frosted-glass screen (it blocks sight, not movement).

Who's where (Read the Room, Wits + Etiquette Diff. 3). Whitmore, “at the back, by the terrace,” beside the north glass doors. Halloway moves through the hall like a host. Voight, alone, on the terrace, checking her watch: “she prefers the terrace because from there she can see who comes in” (from the terrace, through the glass hall, you can see the whole lobby). Thornquist, in the southeast corner of the hall, by the plaza glass, where nobody goes near him. Fry, wherever he likes.

The terrace. Stone paving, railings to the north, west, and east, no lighting of its own: the Fair's tower is visible to the north, off the map. Eavesdrop unseen (Wits + Awareness Diff. 4): on the terrace, Halloway tells a minor Kindred, “The Sheriff is getting old…” The terrace connects to the hall through two glass doors.

The Prince's private salon. Northwest corner: you enter it from the great hall through a wooden door; its north wall is a fixed pane of glass over the terrace, and the west wall another over the plaza. The glass blocks sound but not sight: Whitmore's armchair faces north, toward the terrace and the tower, so from the terrace you can see his lips. This is the LUG-03 detail: with Wits + Awareness Diff. 4, you notice that someone with a telephoto lens, on the terrace, could read lips in the salon. The private audience with the Prince is granted here.

The staff (ghouls, untouchable under the third custom) come out of the pantry in the service block, to the east, carrying the glasses nobody drinks from. The service corridor has a door to the plaza and the stairs to the Keeper's archive, in the basement (map “galeria-archivo”): going down the stairs, the “Down to the archive” region leads to the foot of the basement stairs. Marchetti's apartment (Haven 2) is “above the archive,” on the upper floor of the service block: it has no map.

The curved walls of the 1962 pavilion: the north glass bulges toward the terrace, the plaza panes on either side of the lobby bulge outward, and the private salon has a curved glass bay window to the west. In Foundry each curve is a series of straight glass segments; the two doors to the terrace are two of those segments.

If the Council of A4-E01 moves here (the Prince regained the initiative; Halloway loses 2 dice), it's played in the great hall with a long table brought in by the staff (tile from the tower), or in the private salon if there are only a few of them.

The movable furniture (10) are unlocked tiles: they can be moved, knocked over or used as a barricade.

Placed tokens. Hidden ones are revealed from the token layer; the ones that depend on how the night went say when.
